summary: This bill amends the Social Security Act to prevent the government from recovering Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) overpayments that occurred 10 or more years before the overpayment was discovered.

scores.thoughts: This bill limits the government's ability to recover Social Security and SSI overpayments after 10 years. By reducing the financial burden on beneficiaries who received overpayments, it effectively expands the social safety net by allowing them to retain funds that might otherwise be recouped, thus preventing potential financial hardship.

The bill directly limits the Social Security Administration's ability to recover overpayments after 10 years under Titles II and XVI, forgoing revenue that would otherwise reduce the deficit. This provision is the central and sole purpose of the legislation.
